title: Drone-Delivered Gel Speeds Healing on Ukraine's Front Lines
summary: A gel made in Calgary, Canada, is now helping wounded soldiers and civilians in Ukraine. Drones fly the gel, called NanoSALV Catalytic, to the front lines. NanoTess made it, and Health Canada approved it in 2022. It was first tested by helping unhoused people living in camps, and it is now used for military purposes. The gel is light and does not catch fire. It goes straight onto a wound, and people with little medical training can use it. Since June, it has treated 6,000 wounded soldiers and civilians. Tiny materials in the gel help the body heal faster, use less energy to heal, and fight germs. Hailie Uren, who has worked for four years in eastern Ukraine for the Ukrainian Ministry of Health, says it buys time when one nurse must care for up to 90 patients. NanoTess co-founder and CEO Megan Leslie says the company started with a grant from National Defence in 2020. The gel was also used in Canada after a wildfire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright killed four soldiers and burned dozens more.
why_it_matters: Knowing that simple first aid can help someone while waiting for a doctor matters if you or a friend ever gets hurt at school or on a trip.

keywords.explanation: This is the name of the gel that helps wounds heal faster.
Civilians are ordinary people who are not soldiers.
Unhoused people do not have a home to live in.
The front lines are the places closest to the fighting in a war.
Military purposes means uses connected to soldiers and the armed forces.

background_read: A wound gel is a soft substance that is put straight onto a cut or burn to help it heal.
When many people are hurt at once and nurses are far away, a simple treatment that needs little training can buy time until fuller care arrives.
Drones are small flying machines that can carry supplies quickly to places that are hard to reach.

WHAT: A light gel that is flown by drone to wounds and helps the body heal faster
WHERE: Ukraine's front lines, and Calgary, Canada, where the gel was made
WHY: To help wounded people heal when medical workers are stretched thin and full care is far away
